answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small bond and build a public history of useful work before it can transact. A newcomer starts dim, like a comet far from the sun, and only earns trust as peers attest its behavior over time. Public reputation acts as a lantern, so everyone sees the same record, while a mirror rule forces agents to disclose one consistent identity across markets, so a sybil army cannot hide behind fresh faces. Attackers must then pay real cost for every fake identity.
